title: Signal engine orchestration — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #27 (signal-engine-orchestration), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: analyse() calls evaluate_wave(daily_ohlcv, tide) once directly for today's `wave`, then _wave_showed_state() calls evaluate_wave() again up to 5 times per target state (once for OVERSOLD_PULLBACK, once for OVERBOUGHT_RALLY) -- up to 11 total evaluate_wave() calls per analyse() invocation, each re-deriving the full Stochastic Oscillator/Force Index/rolling-std computations from scratch over its slice. Confirmed via code-review (medium effort) on this PR's diff: evaluate_wave's result never depends on target_state, and since evaluate_wave can only ever produce OVERSOLD_PULLBACK when tide==BULLISH or OVERBOUGHT_RALLY when tide==BEARISH (never both for a given tide), one of the two _wave_showed_state calls is guaranteed to do 5 fully wasted evaluate_wave invocations on every single analyse() call, and the direct `wave` computation duplicates the lookback loop's final (full-length) iteration again on top of that. Not a correctness issue on current single-ticker, on-demand-analysis data sizes (~2-3x cost multiplier on analyse(), which runs once per held/watched ticker), but worth refactoring to compute each lookback bar's wave state once (cache per slice-length, or skip the loop whose target_state can never match the current tide) and check against a single pass instead of two independent loops.

evaluate_impulse(daily_ohlcv) (app/signals/impulse.py, pre-existing) internally computes ema(daily_close, 13) and macd_histogram(daily_close) but only returns the derived GREEN/RED/BLUE color, discarding the series. analyse() then separately recomputes ema(daily_close, 13) and macd_components(daily_close).histogram on the same daily_close for the `indicators` dict this PR added. Both computations produce identical values (same inputs, same functions) but run twice with no sharing -- correctness is unaffected (indicators is independent of evaluate_impulse's return value) but it's real duplicated work introduced by this PR now that analyse() needs those series for a second purpose. Consider having evaluate_impulse optionally accept/return the underlying EMA(13)/MACD-Histogram series (or restructure so engine.py computes them once and passes them to both evaluate_impulse and the indicators dict) next time impulse.py or engine.py is touched.

decisions.decision: Replaced app/signals/engine.py's `_wave_showed_state(daily_ohlcv, tide, target_state)` (called twice per analyse(), once per target state) with a single `_wave_lookback(daily_ohlcv, tide) -> (wave, wave_showed_pullback, wave_showed_rally)` that makes one pass. It (a) derives the single achievable target_state from tide up front (None for NEUTRAL) and skips the lookback loop entirely for the direction that can never match instead of scanning it anyway, (b) reads today's `wave` off the same evaluate_wave call the 'shows' check already needed (rather than a separate direct call), and (c) scans the remaining lookback window newest-to-oldest with an early break on first match, rather than a fixed 5-call scan. Worst case is now 5 evaluate_wave() calls (a directional tide with no match anywhere in the window) and best case 1 (today's bar already matches, or tide is NEUTRAL) -- down from a fixed 11 every time. Rejected caching every lookback bar's wave state across analyse() calls (e.g. a module-level or per-ticker cache keyed by slice length): daily_ohlcv slices change on every new bar/ticker in practice, so a cross-call cache would need invalidation logic disproportionate to the actual cost (a few extra Stochastic/Force Index computations over short slices), and the single-pass-plus-skip approach already eliminates the guaranteed-wasted half of the work the checklist item flagged.
decisions.rationale: Directly addresses the checklist's 'skip the loop whose target_state can never match the current tide' and 'compute each lookback bar's wave state once ... single pass instead of two independent loops' suggestions, while preserving evaluate_wave's existing per-call semantics (no change to Screen 2's own logic) and keeping the function pure/stateless so behavior stays identical to before -- only call count changes. Verified via unit tests in tests/unit/signals/test_engine.py::TestWaveLookback that assert both the returned booleans/wave dict and, where relevant, the exact evaluate_wave call count (e.g. NEUTRAL tide calls it exactly once).

decisions.decision: Gave app.signals.impulse.evaluate_impulse a new optional `histogram: pd.Series | None = None` keyword parameter (mirroring the existing `ema_13` parameter added by portfolio-exit-rules-followups), used in place of an internal macd_histogram(daily_close) call when supplied. app/signals/engine.py's analyse() now computes daily_close's ema_13/ema_26/histogram series once, up front, and passes ema_13/histogram into evaluate_impulse as well as reusing them for the `indicators` dict and (for ema_13) the Elder-Ray Bull/Bear Power calls -- rather than evaluate_impulse recomputing its own ema(13)/macd_histogram internally and analyse() separately recomputing the same series a second time for `indicators`. Rejected restructuring evaluate_impulse to return the series instead of just the GREEN/RED/BLUE color: that would change its return type/contract for every existing caller (including app.portfolio.exits.evaluate_exit_flags, which only wants the color), whereas an additional optional input parameter is purely additive and backward-compatible -- every other call site (evaluate_exit_flags's `evaluate_impulse(daily_ohlcv, ema_13=daily_ema_13)`) is unaffected.
decisions.rationale: Matches the checklist's own suggested fix ('have evaluate_impulse optionally accept/return the underlying EMA(13)/MACD-Histogram series') and the precedent already set by the ema_13 parameter from portfolio-exit-rules-followups, keeping the sharing mechanism consistent across both signal-engine callers. Verified the two computations are provably identical (same fast/slow/signal params, same daily_close input -- app.indicators.macd.macd_histogram is a thin wrapper over macd_components(...).histogram) so no output value changes, only call count; confirmed via the full backend suite (454 tests, 99.83% coverage) and a dedicated TestEvaluateImpulsePrecomputedHistogram class (mirroring the existing TestEvaluateImpulsePrecomputedEma13) added in tests/unit/signals/test_impulse.py for the new histogram parameter path.

review.notes: Full backend suite: 454 passed, 99.83% coverage (90% gate met); app/signals/engine.py and app/signals/impulse.py both at 100% line/branch coverage, matching the PR description's own numbers. No lint/type checker configured in backend/pyproject.toml, so none invented/run. No frontend exists yet and no API route/schema changed, so no OpenAPI/browser-walkthrough concerns -- this PR has no UI surface. Traced _wave_lookback's 'skip the direction the tide can never produce' optimization against evaluate_wave's own source (app/signals/triple_screen.py: OVERSOLD_PULLBACK only ever gated on tide=='BULLISH', OVERBOUGHT_RALLY only ever gated on tide=='BEARISH', with tide held fixed across the whole call, same as the old _wave_showed_state pair) and against docs/Analyse.md Sec.2's tide-conditioned Wave definition -- confirmed genuinely unreachable, not just empirically unobserved. Independently verified equivalence by reimplementing the old _wave_showed_state verbatim and running it head-to-head against the new _wave_lookback over 2000 randomized daily_ohlcv frames x 3 tide values (6000 checks, including n=0 and NEUTRAL-tide edges): zero mismatches on both the showed-pullback/showed-rally booleans and the full wave dict (NaN-aware). Confirmed app.indicators.macd.macd_histogram is a thin wrapper returning the exact same macd_components(...).histogram engine.py now computes directly (same defaults), so no float-precision/ordering risk between evaluate_impulse's gate use and the indicators dict; confirmed the one other evaluate_impulse caller (app/portfolio/exits.py:165) is untouched and still omits the new histogram param. Ran the code-review skill (medium effort) independently against the diff: no findings. decisions entries present and substantive for both changes. No non-blocking findings this pass -- no follow-up task filed.
